en: Visiting every one of them,
Had seen wild beasts and deserts.
In his search for Manas
He had seen peoples of countless kinds.
To the earth's far end, Zhelpinish,
Your accomplished Bakay had traveled.
“Hearing Manas's fame,
I have longed for him.
I traversed the whole earth;
Throughout the whole wide world
I have wandered for twelve years.
I have encountered you unexpectedly.
Are you enemy or friend,
You who have appeared before me?
O my child, what is your battle cry, who are you?
What is your lineage, what is your village?
Thick-armed, with a heart of stone,
You have a winged steed beneath you.
The eighteen thousand worlds
You have the power to rule.
The wandering saint called Khizir
Leads your horse by the bit;
Forty invisible saints on your forty sides
Have become your mighty companions.
(There is no people I have not seen,
There is no land I have not reached.)
Your very head looks different.
When I observe all your limbs,
A wrestler's bearing shows.
You look as though upon your opponents
You have brought slaughter.
Riding alone, seeking a land,
That is how you seem to have been left.
You are my champion, my support;
Tell me your people's battle cry.
O my child, from where have you come, my warrior?”
When Bakay said this,
Manas stood and spoke:
“Finding neither champion nor people,
To make my companion at my side,
Finding no lion equal to myself!
I am the leopard himself,
Who cannot drink his fill of blood;
Of blood-stained Manas the wolf-man
I am the seeing black eye.
I left my Altay land.
I shattered, before leaving Altay,
My Manzhuu and Chinese people.
If you ask about my circumstances,
When I reached twelve
I attacked a mighty nation.
I am the blood-drinker himself.
From ill-intentioned Jakyp
I, Manas, was born blood-stained;
I am his seeing black eye.
Perhaps you have heard of me:
I am blood-shedding Manas himself.
Where snow never leaves in summer or winter,
Ala-Too is our land.
Who give astounding memorial feasts,
The Kyrgyz are our people!
If you become my companion, warrior,
We shall learn your ways.
Many of our kin have been lost;
We are searching for them!
When God laid it upon our heads,
We bore what He had done.
I have searched especially hard
For kin scattered and reduced to want.
I am leopard Manas himself.
If you wish to make peace,
Let us swear a solemn oath!
I am seeking a warrior;
Whose valor is extraordinary,
I am seeking a lion!
Who will die together with me,
I am seeking my equal.
Like Venus and the Pleiades,
I am seeking one to meet with!
Who will break ranks, spear in hand,
Who will fall to a bullet when fate arrives,
Who will die struck by a musket,
Who will face what the Creator has ordained
When it is laid upon his neck;
If I should chance to fall to a bullet,
Who will not leave my body exposed,
But dig the earth and bury me:
I am seeking a companion.
One man worth a thousand,
I am seeking a tiger!
Who never draws back from death,
Who never turns away from his appointed end,
Who, seeing an enemy come against him,
Bristles like a lion,
Who receives wisdom from the unseen:
I am seeking a hero.
Who has girded his waist completely,
Who, if seventy thousand troops come,
Attacks alone into their midst:
I am seeking a champion.
Who never releases what he charges,
Who cannot drink his fill of blood:
I am seeking a blood-stained warrior.
Who says of himself, ‘I am a warrior,’
I am seeking one who knows it!
Make your Quran ready;
If you wish to wage war,
Prepare your sword like this.
Who never draws back when charging,
Of the black Chinese and Manzhuu
Not one champion has returned.
I am the champion, I am the lion;
If you play the warrior,
I am the warrior to satisfy your craving!
I migrated away from Altay.
Against a seething people
I fought six months without rest.
My courage is mighty, my wrath fierce;
I know the measure of myself.
Sharing death, united in life,
If there is a warrior greater than myself,
To make him my true companion,
I am asking after him.
I have many dark, rugged mountains,
Who pierce lungs and cut off heads,
I have many implacable foes.
On the ridges to the north
Are the Kyzylbash and Khiva;
I have many enemies to fight to destruction.
To the east lies the land of Beijing;
Before me are the Baran.
When I consider my own situation,
I have many enemies to contend with.
I know a warrior's circumstances.
Who will thrust the spear alongside me,
Who will scout alongside me,
Who will wage war alongside me,
If hosts of enemies arise,
If a sorrowful dispute arises,
Before one can utter a word,
In the opening and closing of an eye,
Who will turn everything upside down
And drive them out: I seek such a man.
If you ask about my circumstances,
My father was sent into exile,
Wandering helplessly, finding no way out.
Into the hands of the black Kalmyks and Manzhuu
I had fallen.
Fallen where no mortal could escape,
Among the terribly powerful Chinese,
In their domain I had remained.
Where no people traveled, no nation looked,
I had remained in the wilderness.
Of the Kalmyks who claimed us as their own,
I had fallen into their calamity.
When we lived in Altay,
Lashing out, saying, ‘You are Burut,’
Their children raised mocking songs.
When I reached twelve years old,
Their levy brought a quarrel.
I had no champion, no support;
I stood anxious and forlorn.
I had none to match me,
With no horns upon my head,
I had become hornless.
Seeking, I could find no companion;
Then through loneliness
I had become desolate.
If there were a renowned man, a support,
A warrior to bind about my waist,
I would spread my wings.
If an enemy came out to fight,
I would make a memorable deed.
Finding no champion, no support,
I am champion Manas himself.
My trust is in my faith.
Of blood-stained leopard Manas
I am the seeing black eye!”
After Manas said this,
His elder Bakay the wolf-man's
Mustache drooped.
Unable to contain his joy,
Tears flowing from both eyes
Poured down below his collarbones.
Quickly invoking Baabedin,
To Almighty God
Quickly uttering every wish,
Toward the white-gray mare he led,
Leopard Bakay stepped up;
He seized her by the nape.
Holding her motionless then,
Making the gray mare gurgle,
He offered her as a sacrifice.
Without first throwing that mare down,
He cut off her head.
When he saw the white-gray mare,
After lion Bakay had slaughtered her,
Your blood-stained warrior, ready to fight,
Your rash and crafty man,
Now stood utterly amazed.
It turned out to be Bakay himself,
The wolf-man's own black eye;
For the falcon, wolf-man Manas,
He had been searching all this time.
Then Bakay said these words,
Unknown to any round-headed mortal,
He told an exceedingly wondrous tale:
“Manas, because of you
I lost the freshness of my face;
I traveled through many cities.
I wore my blue-gray winged steed to his knees;
Where men had heard, but no people had seen,
I searched, ranging through the land.
My accomplished one, I knew of you.
‘May I reach him and find him,’
I had been praying.
My mighty one, I yearned for you.
I, Bakay, touched by Khizir,
Searched through many places.
If you ask about my circumstances,
Khan Bakay, Bay's son,
Who rinsed his mouth with honey:
At the earth's far end, Zhelpinish,
In Zhelpinish I was born.
A mother came to me from the unseen;
Let me tell it without omission:
To Bakay, endowed with sacred power,
So much precious favor was granted.
The red spear, Joybolot,
I was Bakay who brandished it.
Bringing slaughter through many lands,
I was Bakay who pressed forward.
For champions who girded their loins,
I was Bakay, their support.
More knowing than mortal men,
I am Bakay the lion.
Do not be astonished, my Manas.
The Prophet is true, my religion true;
I gathered those who wandered the wilderness.
What I desired was my faith.
Spending my life's strength,
Leaving all my livestock behind,
I have been searching for Manas.
When I lived in Zhelpinish,
My resting place was a grove of plane trees.
Bakay was born to happiness;
He enjoyed many pleasures.
The fat little fish in the milk lake
Leapt up like butter.
My parrot sang in the willow;
My nightingale warbled its speech.
Possessing all of these,
I was a great lord and a khan.
My sacred power there
Was as great as Ala-Too.
